why:
`rclcpp::NodeOptions::allow_undeclared_parameters` -- REFUSE-LOUD, per-CONCEPT with the rest of the option family (`cpp:NodeOptions` carries the reasoning; this row carries the SITE).

SITE: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/options.hpp:278` (setter) and `:282` (getter). Each is a `template <typename T = void>` whose body is `static_assert(detail::refuse<T>::value, NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_NODE_OPTIONS)` -- dependent on `T` so it fires on USE, not on include, and a caller writes the chain exactly as upstream does. Probe: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_refuse_node_options_probe.cpp`.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: COMPILE ERROR at the call carrying the constraint and the alternative. For this member: the parameter store is fixed-capacity and `declare_parameter<T>(name, default)` is the only way a name enters it -- an undeclared name has no storage to land in.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06): this member used to INHERIT its disposition from `cpp:NodeOptions` and had no row of its own, which is how a live refusal stayed invisible to the ledger -- a refusal is a declaration, it correlates `same`, and `--check` stopped asking. A refusal site now gets its own row so `--require-disposition` can see it.
